title: The Fort Gates Open and the Storming Begins

blocks.text: Facing starvation and siege, the Sikhs prepared for martyrdom instead of waiting passively for death inside the fort. They opened the gates with swords drawn and came out as fighters, determined to meet the attack in the open rather than perish unseen.

The Mughals rushed in expecting treasure and an easy victory, swelling around the fort in overwhelming numbers. The page emphasizes the imbalance—four lakhs against four thousand—while also contrasting Mughal cries of Ali Ali with Sikh cries of Guru Guru at the gate.

Dust, crowding, and greed quickly disordered the attackers, but the defenders still had to fight against impossible odds. The summary preserves the instant when a siege turned into a contested storming and the Singhs met the invasion head-on.
